Subject: Follow-up: DPA clarifications from today's discovery call - Acme Payments

Hi Jenna / Tom,

Thanks again for your time this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on: 

1) Recap:
- Goals: integrate Redwood inference to route transaction risk scoring into your payments flow (low latency, <200ms 99p).
- Data types: tokenized transaction payloads + small amount of user metadata (name/phone/email) for enrichment; sensitive PAN data is redacted upstream.
- Primary ask today: confirmation on data controls, DPA terms, and evidence for SOC 2 and logging.

2) Next steps (what I'm doing):
- Looping in Legal & Security to answer DPA questions and confirm processor/subprocessor posture.
- Sharing our baseline DPA and SOC 2 snapshot for your review (attached).
- If acceptable, we can route the DPA to your contracting system or provide a DocuSign link.

3) Specific clarifications you asked about — please confirm if I captured these correctly:
A) Controller vs. processor: Acme Payments will be the controller; Redwood will be the processor. Confirm?
B) Subprocessors: need list and 30 days notice for additions.
C) Breach notice: required timeline (you asked about 72 hours in the call).
D) Data residency: need US-only hosting for payment data.
E) Data retention & logs: retention windows for PII and audit/log access (ability to produce access logs and deletion upon request).

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Baseline.pdf, SOC2_Report_Redacted.pdf (redacted snapshots).

If that looks right, I'll have Marissa (Legal) and Rishi (Security) provide answers on A–E and propose any minor edits.

Thanks —
Ben

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and you captured the items well. A few follow-ups / clarifications from our side: 

- A) Yes, Acme Payments is the controller. We need contractual language that states Redwood is a processor and that we retain ultimate control over what data is processed.
- B) Subprocessors: we prefer at least 30 days' notice and the ability to object to new subprocessors that will handle PII. Is that in your standard DPA?
- C) Breach notice: our compliance team expects notification within 72 hours of discovery for incidents involving PII. Any faster is welcome — we just need that commitment in writing.
- D) Data residency: all production processing for Acme must remain within US regions (no EU/APAC fallback). Is it possible to pin us to a US-only region?
- E) Retention & logs: we need options to configure data retention and to request deletion; also require access logs for administrative access and a mechanism to produce them for audits.

Finally, please confirm whether Redwood performs any secondary uses of the data for model training or product analytics. That needs to be explicitly disallowed in the DPA for our use-case.

Appreciate the quick turn here. If we can get the DPA clarifications this week, procurement can move to countersign.

Best,
Jenna Lee
Head of Compliance, Acme Payments
jenna.lee@acmepayments.com

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear list. Below are our responses and the proposed next steps. I'm attaching an updated DPA that reflects the processor/controller language and the security commitments discussed.

Responses (short):
A) Roles: Confirmed — Acme Payments = Controller; Redwood Inference = Processor. The attached DPA has explicit language stating Redwood processes Customer Data only per Customer instructions.

B) Subprocessors: We maintain a public subprocessors list (link below) and provide 30 days' notice for material additions. For subprocessors that handle PII, we will notify you and provide an objection window consistent with the balance of the DPA. See attachment 'Subprocessors_list_2026-11-12.csv' for current vendors.

C) Breach notice: Our security policy requires initial notification of confirmed incidents affecting Customer Data as soon as practicable. For incidents involving PII, we commit to an initial notification within 72 hours of confirmation of a security incident. We will provide updates as the investigation proceeds. The DPA has a 72-hour clause for initial notification.

D) Data residency: We can pin your account to US-only regions for production processing and storage. That will be captured in the provisioning config and in the SOW. We will not route Acme data to EU/APAC regions without prior written consent.

E) Retention & logs: 
- Customer Data: retention is configurable. By default, we retain inference logs (non-payload telemetry) for 90 days.
- PII/Requestable deletion: Redwood supports Data Subject Access Requests and deletion upon customer instruction; the DPA includes an article on deletion timelines and proof of deletion.
- Administrative/Audit logs: We provide access logs for admin actions and a mechanism to export them for audits (available via the Console or on-request export).

F) Secondary use / training: We do not use Customer Data or derivatives for model training, ranking, or product analytics unless explicitly agreed in writing and opt-in at the account level. The DPA contains a prohibition on using customer content for training by default.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (proposed edits), Subprocessors_list_2026-11-12.csv, SOC2_Report_Redacted.pdf (from earlier).

Next steps:
- Please review Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf and call out any redlines. We can (A) accept your redlines, (B) route our standard DPA through DocuSign, or (C) provide a countersigned SOW that references the DPA.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a short legal-to-legal call to walk through specific clauses.

If that works, Ben and I will coordinate getting the DPA into DocuSign this week so procurement can move forward.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
